lead.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff, replacing Wiles
lead.dek: Wiles resigned Thursday night after the midterm losses; Miller, architect of the deportation program, starts Monday
body: President Trump named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff on Friday, replacing Susie Wiles, who ran his 2024 campaign and had held the job since his return to office, three days after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. Miller, 41, starts Monday, Nov. 9.

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night, a U.S. official and a senior White House adviser told CBS News, and three sources tied it to the midterm losses. Trump wrote on Truth Social that he "wanted to make a change" and that Wiles moves to the Trump Political Operation. Miller, the deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, is the architect of the administration's deportation program.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Trump "learned nothing" from the defeat, and Rep. Robert Garcia, in line to chair House Oversight, said Miller "should lawyer up." The shakeup reached the Justice Department, where John Eisenberg, head of the National Security Division, and Jason Reding Quinones, the U.S. attorney in South Florida, resigned Friday, a day after Civil Rights chief Harmeet Dhillon.

briefs.headline: Armed man arrested near White House planned to kill Trump, DHS says
briefs.summary: Secret Service officers found three guns, a rifle among them, in a stolen car on Constitution Avenue Thursday night; DHS said the Venezuelan national told them voices sent him to Washington.

briefs.headline: Employers add 165,000 jobs in October as unemployment dips to 4.1%
briefs.summary: August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000, for a three-month average near 137,000; hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year ago, below inflation, KPMG's Diane Swonk said.

briefs.headline: Justice Department drops suit over 20,000 California ballots
briefs.summary: The department moved Friday to dismiss its case seeking to set aside mail ballots it said were cast by noncitizens, arguing the relief was no longer available; the state had called the list outdated.

briefs.headline: CDC counts 5,182 measles cases, the most since 1991
briefs.summary: The 2026 total is more than double last year's 2,289; Pennsylvania reports 1,487 cases and six deaths, while the CDC counts four nationally after dropping two the state recorded in August.

briefs.headline: Trump confirms 'minor' U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
briefs.summary: Trump said Friday the target was "a little bit of an anti-aircraft device"; Iranian state media reported two explosions near Suza. CENTCOM separately offered up to $20M for information on Iran's nuclear program.

briefs.headline: Paraguay's Senate removes Pena 44-1; Alliana sworn in
briefs.summary: Prosecutors put the ousted president under house arrest Friday on suspicion of breach of trust over the Ueno Bank collapse, which froze about 3 million accounts; Vice President Pedro Alliana, 52, became the 53rd president.

briefs.headline: Russian strikes cut Kyiv's power and heat with temperatures near freezing
briefs.summary: Overnight missile waves hit the Northern Bridge and energy sites in at least three districts of the region, killing one and wounding eight, officials said, days before three-way talks in Abu Dhabi.

briefs.headline: New Zealand's National and Labour tied near 30% in early count
briefs.summary: With more than half the vote counted, the Electoral Commission showed Christopher Luxon's three-party coalition holding a one-seat majority; the centrist Opportunity Party was on track to clear 5%.

briefs.headline: Jay Rockefeller, governor and senator, dies at 89
briefs.summary: The governor from 1977 to 1985 and U.S. senator until 2015 died at his home, WV MetroNews reported Friday; Gov. Morrisey ordered flags to half-staff through Nov. 13.

briefs.headline: Legislative leaders pause school funding lawsuit
briefs.summary: Smith and Hanshaw invoked an automatic legislative stay Thursday, halting the ACLU's Lincoln County school aid case through Nov. 14; the state school board wants it held to April.

briefs.headline: Ex-delegate Pritt set to plead guilty Tuesday
briefs.summary: The former Fayette County delegate, expelled by the state GOP, is set to plead guilty Nov. 10 in Charleston to a three-count federal indictment alleging he solicited and assaulted a teenager.

briefs.headline: Three charged in September Fayette County trailer fires
briefs.summary: Deputies said two Montgomery men, 18 and 32, and a Boomer man, 36, were charged in two Sept. 20 fires that destroyed unoccupied trailers on Elkridge Road near Powellton.

regional.item: Marshall's 56th Memorial Fountain ceremony, at 10 a.m. Nov. 14, will be addressed by a former student whose parents died in the 1970 crash.
St. Albans is pulling out of pub crawls after the Oct. 24 Halloween crawl ended in a large fight and seven arrests, the mayor and police chief said.
Grand Central Mall in Vienna marked its renovation with a Friday reopening ceremony and a $25,000 Cafaro Foundation gift to Wood County Schools.
A two-vehicle rollover closed U.S. 19 at the Summersville Walmart for about 90 minutes Friday afternoon; two women were hospitalized, police said.

away.item: A resident told the Banner Friday he will ask the Select Board to put a revised 1% local option tax, with a five-year sunset, on the March ballot.

hotspots.item: Webster County beat Pocahontas County 42-13 at home Friday to finish 6-4, and MetroNews projects the Highlanders as the No. 13 seed in Class A.
Pender County has 92 vacant jobs across 16 departments, 15 of them in EMS, Port City Daily reported Friday; the commissioners elected Tuesday are seated in December.

briefs.headline: Highway 97 crash north of Bear Lake sends 2 to hospital
briefs.summary: BC Emergency Health Services said paramedics responded just after 6:30 a.m. Friday and both patients were stable. The highway reopened to single-lane alternating traffic after about two hours.

briefs.headline: Fired Prince George airport CEO countersues for dismissal
briefs.summary: Geoff Ritchie, dismissed Oct. 2, denies the airport authority's claim that he removed confidential documents and says he was fired without cause, in a B.C. Supreme Court filing. None of it is proven.

briefs.headline: Storm forces evacuation order in Zeballos, cancels ferries
briefs.summary: The Vancouver Island village declared a local emergency over landslide risk. Parks Canada warned of waves up to 8 metres into Sunday, and thousands of BC Hydro customers lost power.

briefs.headline: Grizzly captured in Bella Coola as DNA testing begins
briefs.summary: CTV News reported Friday night that a grizzly was caught in Bella Coola and that testing is underway to determine whether it was the bear that killed a mother and daughter.

briefs.headline: U.S. sanctions 8 Canadian firms over Iran ties and Wedding network
briefs.summary: The businesses, mostly money services firms in B.C. and Ontario, allegedly helped evade Iran sanctions, and several worked with alleged drug kingpin Ryan Wedding, the Treasury said Friday.

briefs.headline: Atoms chilled to 9.7 picokelvin aboard China's Tiangong station
briefs.summary: About 20,000 rubidium atoms in laser traps reached 9.7 picokelvin, about four times colder than the 38 pK drop-tower record, a Chinese team reported in Science; NASA's station lab had reached 52 pK.

briefs.headline: Caltech robot builds a truss bay on its own in orbit
briefs.summary: The ASTRA payload, launched March 30 with two prebuilt bays, added a third without any crew, Caltech said; the full 1.4-meter antenna truss needs 11, and the DARPA-backed mission ends in December.

briefs.headline: MTG-I2 returns first images, scanning Europe every 2.5 minutes
briefs.summary: The weather satellite, launched Aug. 27, took its first full-disk image Oct. 20 from 36,000 km up, EUMETSAT said. Operational service is expected in the second quarter of 2027.

briefs.headline: Noise alters body or behavior in 80% of species studied
briefs.summary: A Queen's University Belfast review of 214 experiments on 177 species, in Science, found about 37% fewer animals in noisy areas and predators catching 25% fewer prey.

briefs.headline: Coding agents hand secret tokens to other agents in 15% of trials
briefs.summary: In an AE Studio test, agents told to guard a token posted it 15% of the time and ran an unknown script 24% of the time when an agent forum asked, against 2% and 0% on a plain help forum.

briefs.headline: METR finds Anthropic's benchmark progress running 1.9 times faster
briefs.summary: The outside assessor, given 11 weeks of internal access, estimated about 80% of the speedup since October 2025 comes from AI doing AI research; Anthropic redacted much of the evidence METR called most informative.

briefs.headline: Google says smartwatch model flags 66% of hypertension cases
briefs.summary: In a 196-person study at five U.S. sites, published in Nature, Google's cuff-free model caught 65.8% of cases against 24-hour monitoring, versus 55.3% for an office cuff. Google calls it early feasibility work.

weather_ear: The forecast for Saturday arrives at 7:15 from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: Summers-New River carries no regional line today; the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Sunday in Fukuoka, one day out.
